Executive Summary
The JI CUSTOM FIELD Service represents the software component that has been defined for the implementation of the JAGGAER Indirect Solution via FTP for custom fields.
The following topics describe the JI CUSTOM FIELD Service:
1. CSV Import Service
2. Import Data Format: Describes the list of files required to perform proper import functionality.
3. Import Result Response: Describes the structure of the CSV file generated with operation responses.
For a description of possible service configuration settings, refer to the main JINT FTP File Service documentation.
CSV Import Service
This service enables custom field objects to be imported into the JAGGAER Indirect Solution.
The following operations are allowed for each type of object that can be imported:
These operations must be performed using the following sequence:
1. DELETE Custom Field Relationship
2. DELETE Custom Field Value
Note: If a relationship exists for the value, you must delete the relationship before you can delete the value.
1. MODIFY Custom Field Value
2. MODIFY/DELETE WF Dynamic Rule
3. ADD Custom Field Relationship
When the service starts, it searches the following folder structure on the FTP server:

Starting from the root folder, the system searches for an initial folder whose name starts with the prefix specified in the rootDataFolderName configuration parameter. (By default, the value JICUSTOMFIELDDATA is used for the JI CUSTOM FIELD Service.) Note that JICUSTOMFIELDDATA is the prefix. The folder name can be longer and include other characters after the prefix.

Once the system finds the starting folder, it looks for a subfolder whose name starts with “CREATE_UPDATE”. (Again, the name can contain other characters at the end.). Only files that are stored in this folder are considered.

Files in the CREATE_UPDATE folder are used to both create/update objects (custom field values with approvers and business units, workflow dynamic rules, custom field relationships) and delete custom field values or wf dynamic rules or custom field relationships.
Files are recognized by the final part of their name, so the full name doesn't matter. What is important is that files end with the defined postfix and extension (case-insensitive).
The following table lists expected file names and how they are used.
Import Data Format
This topic describes the datasets that can be retrieved from the JI CUSTOM FIELD Service import files.
Note: In the following tables, the names of mandatory fields are bold.
CFVALUE.CSV and CFVALUEDEL.CSV [CSV Import Service]
These files contain information about custom field values to be modified (CFVALUE.CSV) or deleted (CFVALUEDEL.CSV).
CFVAPPROVER.CSV [CSV Import Service]
This file contains the list of approver users related to the custom field value.
CFVBU.CSV [CSV Import Service]
This file contains the list of business units assigned to the custom field value.

Note: Whatever the component of the custom field you want to update, if the custom field value has an existing business unit associated with it, this file must always be provided; otherwise, the existing business unit will be removed.
CFVWFVRULEMOD.CSV and CFVWFVRULEDEL.CSV [CSV Import Service]
These files contain the list of WF dynamic rules related to the custom field value that are to be modified (CFVWFVRULEMOD.CSV) or deleted (CFVWFVRULEDEL.CSV).
CFVWFAPPROVER.CSV [CSV Import Service]
This file contains the list of approver users related to the WF dynamic rule.
CFRELATIONSHIPMOD.CSV and CFRELATIONSHIPDEL.CSV [CSV Import Service]
These files contain information about custom field relationships to be modified (CFRELATIONSHIPMOD.CSV) or deleted (CFRELATIONSHIPDEL.CSV).
Import Result Response
You may encounter two kinds of files reporting import service errors:
1. Error Encountered while Parsing Source File
2. Error Found while Executing Import
Error Encountered while Parsing Source File

When reading source data, there may be an error in the format of the data inserted into the file. For example, mandatory fields might have been left empty or the data format might be wrong. When this happens, a file is created that lists the encountered errors, and operation on the whole custom field identified by the corresponding OBJ_KEY value is not performed. The user is then asked to correct the source file and to resubmit the data to repeat the operation.
The name of the file is in the form:
<filePrefixMask>_<name of processed file>Result.csv
For example, if an error is found in the CFVALUE.CSV file, the error is reported in a file with a name like:
20200220_1200_customField_CFVALUEResult.CSV
The file will contain the following fields:
Error Found while Executing Import
If files have been parsed successfully, the read data is used to call the JAGGAER Indirect Solution to perform the operation. The result of each call is then collected and written in a file.
The name of the file is in the form:
<filePrefixMask><rootDataFolderName>_<operation performed>.csv
For example, responses for a CREATE_UPDATE operation are reported in a file with a name like:
20200208_1200_customFieldJICUSTOMFIELDDATA_CREATE_UPDATE.csv
For a DELETE operation, the file will be:
20200208_1200_customFieldJICUSTOMFIELDDATA_DELETE.csv
